observation.visible_scene: A flat, tan-colored piece of material lies on sandy ground, its center and left side blackened and charred while the right portion remains unburnt tan. Open yellow-orange flames burn along the left edge and along a folded right edge of the piece. The surrounding ground shows sand, scattered small pebbles, dark burnt fragments, and a pile of grey ash at the right edge of the frame. The camera viewpoint is fixed; background elements keep the same positions throughout.
visible_changes: The two main flame tongues continuously flicker, change height, and bend in shape without the object itself moving; the left flame alternates between short upright tongues (e.g., frame 6) and long stretched horizontal streaks pointing up-left (e.g., frames 36-40).
The right flame likewise shifts between tall vertical forms and shorter, curved or split shapes across the frames.
Small isolated glowing orange/red embers appear intermittently to the left of and above the burning piece (e.g., frames 3, 5, 10, 11, 16, 39) and are absent in neighboring frames.
The tan unburnt surface and the black charred region retain roughly the same overall outline and position on the ground, with no visible translation or large deformation of the piece itself.
The ash pile, pebbles, and scattered debris on the ground remain stationary, indicating no camera motion.
Combustion is already ongoing at the first frame and is still ongoing at the last frame; no ignition or extinguishing occurs within the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause or start of the burning, the identity/composition of the material, and what happens to the flames and charred piece after the segment ends are not shown.
Whether the blackened area is growing over time cannot be confirmed from this short crop.
uncertain_details: Whether the brief orange/red specks are airborne embers, sparks, or separate small objects is not fully resolvable.
Subtle changes in the size of the charred region versus simple flame occlusion are hard to distinguish.
